items.reason: The book's printed answer is the two filled diagrams (55, 10, 40, 25 and 16, 7, 13, 10); the answer is itself the figure.

diagram.manim_description: Canvas 16:9 on BG, scene units 16 wide by 9 high, origin at the centre, x to the right, y up. Draw two star diagrams side by side: the left star centred at (-4.2, 0) and the right star centred at (4.2, 0). In each star the centre box is a rectangle 1.6 wide by 1.0 high drawn with an INK outline of 3 px and BG fill, holding the expression in INK at text height 0.45 (left star: 5u with the letter u in italics; right star: 5 + u with u in italics). Around it sit four corner boxes, each a rectangle 1.6 wide by 1.1 high with an INK outline of 3 px and BG fill, whose centres lie at offsets (-2.5, +2.3) top-left, (+2.5, +2.3) top-right, (-2.5, -2.3) bottom-left and (+2.5, -2.3) bottom-right from the star's centre. From each corner of the centre box an INK arrow of 3 px runs diagonally outwards to the nearest corner of the matching corner box with its arrowhead at the corner box: top-left arrow from (-0.8, +0.5) to (-1.7, +1.75), top-right from (+0.8, +0.5) to (+1.7, +1.75), bottom-left from (-0.8, -0.5) to (-1.7, -1.75), bottom-right from (+0.8, -0.5) to (+1.7, -1.75), all offsets from the star's centre. Beside each arrow place an INK label at text height 0.4 with u in italics: top-left arrow label u = 11 centred at (-2.4, +0.95), top-right arrow label u = 2 centred at (+2.2, +0.95), bottom-left arrow label u = 8 centred at (-2.2, -0.95), bottom-right arrow label u = 5 centred at (+2.2, -0.95), all offsets from the star's centre; both stars use the same four labels in the same four places. Fill state of the corner boxes (every box is filled): left star, top-left (u = 11) shows 55, top-right (u = 2) shows 10, bottom-left (u = 8) shows 40, bottom-right (u = 5) shows 25; right star, top-left (u = 11) shows 16, top-right (u = 2) shows 7, bottom-left (u = 8) shows 13, bottom-right (u = 5) shows 10. The two values given in the question, 10 and 7 in the u = 2 boxes, stay in INK; the six values added by the solution (55, 40, 25 in the left star and 16, 13, 10 in the right star) are drawn in ANSWER green. All box text at text height 0.5. Nothing else is drawn.
must_not_show: an equal or not-equal sign, or the words equal and not equal
the arithmetic behind each value such as 5 x 11
the red and blue label colours or the speech marks of the book
accuracy_checks: layout, labels and the two given values are identical to the question diagram
matches the book's printed answer diagrams (55, 10, 40, 25 and 16, 7, 13, 10)
diagram.alt_text: The two star diagrams filled in: 5u gives 55, 10, 40, 25 and 5 + u gives 16, 7, 13, 10 for u = 11, 2, 8, 5.
diagram.render_note: Printed answer of the book (page with answers to p.92). Same layout as the question diagram; new values in ANSWER green.

items.lp_book_number: Example 11: adding the numbers in a picture
items.ncert_ref: Section 4.4 - Example 11: adding the numbers in a picture
items.question_text: A picture has a top row of four copies of 3, then two rows each with one r and one s, and a bottom row of four copies of 3. Add all the numbers in three ways and simplify.
items.reason: The book question is 'the sum of the numbers in the picture'; the three ways (rows, like terms, upper half) are read off the layout of the 4 x 4 tile picture.

content.unit_note: local units, tile centres on a 1.2 spacing, row 1 on top, column 1 on the left

diagram.manim_description: Canvas 16:9 on BG. Use local units with tile centres on a grid of spacing 1.2 (column 1 at x = 0, column 2 at x = 1.2, column 3 at x = 2.4, column 4 at x = 3.6; row 1 at y = 3.6, row 2 at y = 2.4, row 3 at y = 1.2, row 4 at y = 0), and scale the whole drawing so that its bounding box is centred on the canvas with an even margin. Row 1 (top): four squares of side 1.0, each filled MARK_FILL with an INK outline of 2.5 px, each holding the number 3 in INK at text height 0.55. Row 2: a circle of diameter 1.0 filled CELL_FILL with an INK outline of 2.5 px holding the italic letter r in INK at column 1, and a circle of the same size and fill holding the italic letter s in INK at column 2; columns 3 and 4 of row 2 are empty. Row 3: the same as row 2, a circle r at column 1 and a circle s at column 2, columns 3 and 4 empty. Row 4 (bottom): four squares of side 1.0 filled MARK_FILL with an INK outline, each holding the number 3. In all there are 8 squares marked 3, 2 circles r and 2 circles s. Nothing else is drawn.
must_not_show: any sum, total or expression such as 2r + 2s + 24
grouping lines, brackets or colours that mark upper half, rows or like terms
question mark or the words Total
accuracy_checks: 8 tiles show 3 (rows 1 and 4, four each)
2 circles show r (rows 2 and 3, column 1) and 2 circles show s (rows 2 and 3, column 2)
columns 3 and 4 of rows 2 and 3 are empty
total of the picture is 8 x 3 + 2r + 2s = 24 + 2r + 2s (not drawn)
diagram.alt_text: Four tiles marked 3 on top, two rows each holding a circle r and a circle s, and four tiles marked 3 at the bottom.
diagram.render_note: Book figure of Example 11. Squares use MARK_FILL (the book's light green) and the two circles CELL_FILL; the book colours r and s differently, which carries no meaning here. Same picture as the teaching image of the earlier topic (M2.S19.T19.C80.IMG1), but drawn again for this item and never linked.

items.question_text: A picture has a top row of four copies of 3, then two rows each with one r and one s, and a bottom row of four copies of 3. Add all the numbers in three ways and simplify.
items.reason: The three ways of adding (row wise, like terms, upper half doubled) are written as expressions; the picture of tiles would only repeat the question figure and nothing is added to it. A colour-grouped copy of the picture (rows, like terms, upper half) would be a nice extra but is not needed.
